brief: Create a 4-second, 640×360, 24fps motion metaphor called Room to Move. On a pale background, two orange gate panels initially cover a blue square; they slide apart from a named open cue, revealing the square. A pinned-font heading 'Room to move' then arrives, remains readable for at least a second, and fades before the end. Use native timed layers and at least one seconds duration and named marker. Use the repository's pinned font file through the skill's asset API, not a fabricated hash. Keep deliberate stillness for the reading interval.
scope: Two independent agents with no conversation fork, reading only the skill as authoring guidance; no tracked implementation edits.

repairs.change: Initial authoring guessed inFrame/outFrame; unknown native timed field names.
Removed timing to get valid baseline and inspect own exported JSON.
Explicit center anchors; startFrame/endFrame. Diagnostics recognize startFrame, reject endFrame.
Use only native startFrame; valid. Lint exposes startFrame local-time offset and 0.75s reading failure.
Adjust heading motions for local-time offset; reading-time error resolved. Rendered-frame inspection reveals background covers every foreground layer.
Move square and background after foreground layer additions; visual verification succeeds.

visual_checks.result: Orange gate panels cover the blue square.
Orange panels separated; blue square and complete heading visible.
Blue square remains revealed; heading has faded away.

guidance_gaps_observed: Native timed layer field name startFrame is not documented in the skill.
startFrame offsets all animated tracks into local layer time; named marker placement into native timed layers is not explained.
First added layers appear in front; the skill does not describe stacking order.
Default anchor [0,0] is not stated; explicit anchor center is needed for intended solid centering.
Default lint frozen-run threshold conflicts with brief-requested deliberate stillness.

guideRepairs: Name native layer timing fields inPoint/outPoint/startFrame/stretch and explain their clocks.
Explain first-added layers paint in front; use composition background or add backdrops last.
Explain delayed fade-in initial visibility versus placed segment from values.
